note: Hand-written, human-judged cases. `required` are rules that must reach the session; `acceptable` may reach it without counting as false deliveries; every other delivery is a false delivery. Should-not-fire and near-miss cases require nothing and accept nothing. Written before any trigger edit; the split is by sha256(id) in run_eval.py.

cases.why: Reading a repo doc is routine and no taught rule binds a plain read.
Opening a library file to understand it binds nothing.
Reading a JSON config is inspection, not a decision a rule governs.
Searching code for a symbol is a read-only lookup with no rule at stake.
Listing files by glob is routine navigation.
A directory listing changes nothing and binds no rule.
git status is a read-only check of the tree.
git log is a read-only history check.
Peeking at the top of a file is a read.
Running an existing selftest verifies work and creates nothing a rule governs.
A two-word acknowledgement carries no work for a rule to bind.
A where-is-it question about the repo layout is answered by reading.
cases.prompt: Where does the routes file live in the repo?

cases.why: A one-word copy fix is a small edit no doctrine rule governs.
cases.prompt: Fix the typo in the second paragraph of the README.

cases.why: Push notifications on a phone are not git push, so no repo rule binds.
cases.prompt: Turn off push notifications on my phone while I am in the meeting.

cases.why: Merging paragraphs is editing prose, not merging records or a pull request.
cases.prompt: Merge these two paragraphs into one and keep the second sentence.

cases.why: Echoing the words git push prints text and pushes nothing.

tool_input.command: echo 'remember: git push only after review' >> /tmp/notes.txt

cases.why: Searching docs for the phrase git push is a read, not a push.
A general question about how email works does not touch Joe's mail.
cases.prompt: Explain in two sentences how email delivery works between servers.

cases.why: Password length advice is general security knowledge, not a login task.
cases.prompt: How long should a strong password be these days?

cases.why: The word agent in the real estate sense is not a delegated subagent.
cases.prompt: What does the word agent mean in a commercial real estate listing agreement?

cases.why: Briefing a subagent to sweep mail is delegation, which the seat-dispatch and data-class rules govern.

tool_input.prompt: Sweep Joe's mail export for vendor introduction threads and summarize each one.

cases.why: Searching Joe's mail through the Gmail connector is the exact move the local-mail-store rule forbids.
Sending mail from the AI Gmail is governed by the email-handover rule.
Opening a loop is what the deferral-gate rule polices.

tool_input.title: Follow up on the vendor list

cases.why: Confirming a party merge is where the survivorship and lead-vs-client rules bind.
Capturing a taught rule is governed by the would-the-system-have-to-ask-again test.

tool_input.statement: Always name the deal in the question.

cases.why: Writing a new hook file is building a gate, so write-the-test-first binds.
A shared x.com post binds the quoted-post rule and the Grok-first retrieval rule.
cases.prompt: Look at this and tell me what we should steal: https://x.com/someone/status/1234567890

cases.why: A vendor pairing draft is intro-politics work, which the pairing-judgment rules govern.
cases.prompt: Draft an introduction pairing the roofing vendor with the Mobile clinic client.

cases.why: A client note that names HIPAA binds the spelling and double-check rule.
cases.prompt: Draft a short note to the client about HIPAA compliance for the new lease.

cases.why: Asking which LOI terms are negotiable is the LOI-template rule's moment.
cases.prompt: Which terms on the LOI template are actually negotiable?

cases.why: Convening reviewers is the moment the distinct-lenses red-team rule binds.
cases.prompt: Convene a red team of three reviewers for this design.

cases.why: Creating a client record triggers the open-source research rule.
